In languages which abound in consonantal finals, compound consonants are segregated. by the interposition of a vowel between them, the final vowel being occasionally elided; thus in the Hindi, the Sanskrit word ''marma" [a joint] is, by the interposition of an a after the r'and the elision of the final a, converted into maram ; dharam, karam and parab aro instances of the effect of the same rules.
